content: Interventions for managing chronic pelvic pain in women involve a variety of approaches tailored to the underlying cause, if identifiable, and the individual needs of the patient. These may include pharmacological treatments such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief, hormonal therapies like oral contraceptives or gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists to address conditions such as endometriosis, and neuromodulators for neuropathic pain. Surgical options, including laparoscopy, may be considered to diagnose and treat conditions like endometriosis or adhesions. Physical therapy, particularly pelvic floor rehabilitation, can be beneficial for musculoskeletal contributions to pain. Psychological interventions, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), are often recommended to address the emotional and psychological impact of chronic pain. Multidisciplinary approaches that combine medical, surgical, physical, and psychological therapies are frequently employed to optimize outcomes. In some cases, alternative therapies like acupuncture or dietary modifications may also be explored, though evidence for their efficacy varies.
